items.description: Comprehensive codebase audit: catalog every module, data flow, and dependency
items.acceptance_criteria: A structured document (repository_structure.md) listing all Python scripts, their inputs/outputs, the concept_evolve tree structure, and a dependency graph showing how test_harness.py, baseline_*.py, block_evaluator.py, experiment_fast.py, and test_annealed.py connect. Must identify gaps in the existing 22-item rubric (14 completed, 8 pending) and justify why a fresh rubric is needed.

items.description: Web-based literature survey: gather all post-2020 papers on Chvatal-Sankoff constants and LCS bounds
items.acceptance_criteria: At least 15 relevant papers cited in sources.bib with BibTeX entries, including the foundational [CS1975], [DP1995], [D1994], [L2009], [H2024], plus at least 5 new papers not currently in sources.bib (e.g., Tiskin 2022 retracted exact form, Bukh-Cox frog dynamics, Houdre-Lember subadditivity refinements, Amsalu-Matzinger TASEP connections, Li-Ren-Wen 2025 multi-string results). Each entry must have title, authors, year, and DOI/URL.

items.description: Critical analysis of existing bounds techniques: deterministic vs probabilistic vs hybrid
items.acceptance_criteria: A report (bounds_strategies_report.md updated or replaced) that: (a) tabulates all known lower/upper bounds with their proof techniques, (b) identifies why the Heineman lower bound 0.792665992 is currently the tightest deterministic bound, (c) explains why the repo's beam-search bound 0.799682 is NOT a valid improvement over Heineman (it uses finite block N=1000, so subadditivity only guarantees E[LCS]/n >= result for that specific n, not the asymptotic constant), (d) catalogs three concrete attack vectors for tighter bounds.

items.description: Subagent delegation: Concept-tree exploration synthesis and gap identification
items.acceptance_criteria: Deploy concept-tree-explorer subagent to traverse all 10 concept folders in results/concept_evolve/tree/. Produce a synthesis report identifying: (a) which concepts have working code vs. only documentation, (b) which concept paths from walk_paths.json have been experimentally validated, (c) rank concepts by estimated impact on tightening bounds, (d) identify at least 3 unexplored concept combinations.

items.description: Subagent delegation: Literature graph mining for transfer matrix and TASEP connections
items.acceptance_criteria: Deploy literature-graph-miner subagent to mine citation graphs starting from Heineman2024 and Lueker2009. Must return: (a) at least 5 papers connecting LCS to TASEP/KPZ universality, (b) at least 3 papers on transfer matrix methods for sequence alignment, (c) identification of the most promising unexploited technique for tighter bounds. Results stored in results/concept_evolve/tree/ as literature.json updates.

items.description: Formalize the rigorous lower-bound proof framework via subadditivity
items.acceptance_criteria: Document (in results/concept_evolve/tree/ or a new markdown file) the precise mathematical conditions under which a Monte Carlo block estimate yields a valid lower bound on the Chvatal-Sankoff constant. Must address: (a) Kingman's subadditive ergodic theorem requirements, (b) the distinction between E[LCS(n)]/n for finite n vs. the limit gamma_2, (c) why superadditivity of E[LCS] means E[LCS(n)]/n is an UPPER bound on gamma_2 (not lower!), (d) correct interpretation of the beam search result as a heuristic lower bound on E[LCS(n)]/n which in turn lower-bounds gamma_2 only if the beam search provably underestimates the true LCS length.

items.description: Validate and extend exact E[LCS(n)]/n computation to n=18
items.acceptance_criteria: Optimize baseline_exact_lcs.py using Numba or C extension to compute exact E[LCS(n)]/n for n=1..18. Store results as results/exact_lcs_table.json with columns [n, E_LCS, E_LCS_over_n]. Verify n=10 matches existing output. The sequence E[LCS(n)]/n should be monotonically decreasing (since E[LCS] is superadditive, E[LCS(n)]/n decreases to gamma_2), providing exact upper bounds on gamma_2 for small n.

items.description: Implement rigorous Heineman-style deterministic lower bound automaton for small state counts
items.acceptance_criteria: Implement (not stub) the Dancik/Heineman finite automaton lower bound method: (a) define a greedy matching automaton with k-bit memory, (b) build its transition matrix on binary alphabet, (c) compute the stationary distribution, (d) derive the deterministic lower bound as the expected output per step. Must reproduce a known lower bound (e.g., >= 0.7739 for a basic automaton) and store results in results/automaton_lower_bounds.json.

items.description: Implement the annealed upper bound with optimized beta search and verify against Lueker
items.acceptance_criteria: Extend test_annealed.py to: (a) use scipy.optimize.minimize_scalar for optimal beta, (b) compute for N=100,1000,10000,100000 and verify convergence, (c) compare against Lueker's 0.826280. The annealed bound should yield approximately 0.8678 (known to be looser than Lueker). Store results in results/annealed_upper_bound.json. Document why the annealed bound is loose (it ignores correlations in the LCS structure).

items.description: Build unified evaluation harness with standardized bound certification
items.acceptance_criteria: Refactor test_harness.py into a modular evaluation framework that: (a) accepts any bound function with signature (n) -> (bound_value, bound_type, proof_method), (b) logs results with timestamp, parameters, and proof validity flag, (c) automatically compares against the best known bounds from sources.bib, (d) generates a summary table in results/bounds_comparison.json. Must handle both deterministic and probabilistic bounds with appropriate confidence levels.

items.description: Subagent delegation: Validate the beam search lower bound proof chain end-to-end
items.acceptance_criteria: Deploy a general subagent to: (a) re-run block_evaluator.py with M=10000 trials (quick validation), (b) verify the Hoeffding bound calculation is mathematically correct, (c) trace the full proof chain: beam search underestimates LCS -> Hoeffding bounds mean -> superadditivity gives constant bound, (d) identify any logical gaps. Report must explicitly state whether 0.799682 is a valid lower bound on gamma_2 or only on E[LCS(1000)]/1000.

items.description: Develop MDP-based lower bound with larger lookahead K=12..16 using sparse methods
items.acceptance_criteria: Extend experiment_fast.py to handle K=12..16 by: (a) exploiting sparsity in the transition matrix (most state pairs are unreachable), (b) using iterative sparse solvers instead of dense arrays, (c) achieving at least K=14 within 1 hour of computation. Store results in results/mdp_lower_bounds.json. The K=14 bound should exceed K=10's 0.7813. If it surpasses 0.7927 (Heineman), this is a significant result.

items.description: Implement transfer matrix upper bound method inspired by Lueker's alignment graph
items.acceptance_criteria: Implement a transfer matrix approach where: (a) the state encodes the DP frontier profile (difference sequence), (b) the transfer matrix T maps frontier states as a new random character is appended, (c) the leading eigenvalue of T gives E[LCS(n)]/n for the restricted profile. For frontier width w=10..20, compute the eigenvalue and compare to Lueker's 0.826280. Code stored as transfer_matrix_upper.py, results in results/transfer_matrix_upper.json.

items.description: Design and implement a hybrid beam-search + MDP lower bound strategy
items.acceptance_criteria: Create a new lower bound method that combines: (a) the MDP policy for K-bit lookahead to make locally optimal matching decisions, (b) beam search to explore multiple alignment paths simultaneously, (c) Hoeffding concentration over M independent block trials. The hybrid should outperform both pure beam search (0.8034 empirical) and pure MDP (0.7813 at K=10). Implementation in hybrid_mdp_beam.py, results in results/hybrid_lower_bounds.json.

items.description: Concept-tree evolution: explore LP relaxation and dual witness upper bound
items.acceptance_criteria: Create a new concept folder results/concept_evolve/tree/011_lp_dual_witness/ with: (a) concept.json describing the LP relaxation of the LCS problem as a maximum weight matching in the alignment graph, (b) README.md with the mathematical formulation, (c) a prototype lp_upper_bound.py that solves the LP dual for random string pairs of length n=50..200 and extrapolates the ratio, (d) literature.json citing relevant LP/IP approaches to sequence alignment.

items.description: Concept-tree evolution: explore importance sampling with tilted measure for tighter Monte Carlo lower bound
items.acceptance_criteria: Create a new concept folder results/concept_evolve/tree/012_tilted_importance_sampling/ with: (a) concept.json describing how tilting the string distribution toward high-LCS-length pairs reduces variance, (b) a prototype tilted_mc.py that: generates string pairs from a biased distribution favoring longer LCS, applies importance weights to recover the unbiased expectation, and achieves lower variance than the uniform sampling in block_evaluator.py, (c) results.json showing variance reduction factor >= 2x compared to uniform sampling at N=1000.

items.description: Subagent delegation: Rapid prototyping and ranking of all concept-tree approaches
items.acceptance_criteria: Deploy a general subagent to: (a) implement quick proof-of-concept scripts for at least 3 of the 10 existing concept folders that lack working code (e.g., 001_kpz, 003_thermodynamic, 004_cavity, 009_tensor_network), (b) run each for <= 5 minutes, (c) produce a ranked comparison table showing which approach gives the best empirical signal toward tighter bounds, (d) store the ranking in results/concept_evolve/concept_ranking.json.

items.description: Large-scale lower bound computation: beam search with optimized parameters
items.acceptance_criteria: Run block_evaluator.py (or improved version) with: (a) N=5000, W=500, M=100000 as primary configuration, (b) N=2000, W=1000, M=200000 as secondary, (c) N=10000, W=200, M=50000 as tertiary. Store all results in results/large_scale_lower.json. Report the best provable lower bound achieved and compare against Heineman's 0.792665992. The goal is a provable bound > 0.793.

items.description: Upper bound experiments: transfer matrix and LP methods at scale
items.acceptance_criteria: Run the transfer matrix upper bound (item_013) and LP dual witness (item_015) at maximum feasible scale. Store results in results/upper_bound_experiments.json. Report: (a) the tightest upper bound achieved by each method, (b) comparison against Lueker's 0.826280, (c) convergence analysis showing how the bound tightens with increasing problem size. Goal: achieve an upper bound < 0.826.

items.description: Subagent delegation: Automated hyperparameter sweep for beam search and MDP
items.acceptance_criteria: Deploy a general subagent to conduct a systematic grid search over: (a) beam width W in {50, 100, 200, 500, 1000}, (b) block length N in {500, 1000, 2000, 5000}, (c) MDP lookahead K in {8, 10, 12, 14}. For each configuration, run at least M=1000 trials and record (empirical_ratio, lower_bound, runtime). Store results in results/hyperparameter_sweep.json. Identify the Pareto frontier of (bound_tightness, runtime).

items.description: Convergence analysis: extrapolate gamma_2 from finite-n data
items.acceptance_criteria: Using the exact values from item_007 (n=1..18) and Monte Carlo estimates for n=50,100,200,500,1000,2000,5000: (a) fit the Richardson extrapolation model E[LCS(n)]/n = gamma_2 + c/n^alpha, (b) report the extrapolated gamma_2 with confidence interval, (c) compare the extrapolation against the known bounds [0.7927, 0.8263]. Store fitting results and plots data in results/convergence_analysis.json.

items.description: Compare all results against prior work from literature review
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/comparison_with_prior_work.json containing: (a) a table comparing every bound computed in this project against the corresponding prior best from sources.bib, (b) the absolute and relative margin of improvement for each bound, (c) identification of which results are genuinely novel (tighter than all prior work), (d) honest assessment of which results are replication vs. improvement. Must reference at least 8 entries from sources.bib.

items.description: Asymptotic scaling analysis: characterize the rate of convergence of bounds
items.acceptance_criteria: Analyze how each bounding method's tightness scales with computational resources: (a) MDP lower bound vs K (expect logarithmic improvement), (b) beam search lower bound vs W and N (expect sqrt(log) improvement), (c) transfer matrix upper bound vs frontier width (expect exponential convergence to true value). Document scaling laws in results/scaling_analysis.json with fitted exponents.

items.description: Concept-tree final traversal: identify the most productive research path
items.acceptance_criteria: Using all experimental results, update results/concept_evolve/tree/index.json with a 'productivity_score' field for each concept (ratio of bound improvement to computation time). Identify the single most productive concept path and document why it worked. Update adjacency.json with any new edges discovered during experimentation.

items.description: Subagent delegation: Draft research summary with rigorous proofs
items.acceptance_criteria: Deploy a general subagent to produce a LaTeX or Markdown draft (results/research_summary.md) containing: (a) abstract summarizing the tightest new bounds achieved, (b) Section 1: Problem statement citing [CS1975], (c) Section 2: Methods (MDP, beam search, transfer matrix) with full algorithmic descriptions, (d) Section 3: Results table comparing against [H2024] and [L2009], (e) Section 4: Proofs of bound validity (subadditivity argument, Hoeffding inequality, deterministic automaton output), (f) Bibliography referencing all entries in sources.bib. Must be >= 3000 words.

items.description: Final bounds certificate: produce a machine-verifiable proof of the tightest bound
items.acceptance_criteria: For the single tightest new bound (lower or upper), produce results/bound_certificate.json containing: (a) the bound value to 10 decimal places, (b) the proof method (deterministic automaton output / Hoeffding + subadditivity / LP dual), (c) all parameters needed to reproduce (K, W, N, M, random seed if applicable), (d) a verification script verify_bound.py that independently checks the bound by re-running the computation with the same parameters and confirming the result. The verification must complete in < 30 minutes.

items.description: Update README.md and finalize all documentation
items.acceptance_criteria: README.md updated to include: (a) project overview and the Chvatal-Sankoff problem statement, (b) summary of all bounds achieved with references, (c) instructions for reproducing results, (d) directory structure explanation, (e) bibliography section pointing to sources.bib. All results/*.json files must be internally consistent. research_rubric.json summary counts must be accurate.
